definition: Quantify numerical uncertainty in BBH waveforms by comparing outputs at different resolutions and extrapolation orders
assumptions: Waveform differences between resolutions approximate the truncation error
Log-normal distribution is appropriate model for error distributions
Minimal time and phase alignment removes trivial differences
Extrapolation order convergence measures extraction uncertainty
invariants: Higher resolution should yield more accurate waveforms
Dominant (ell=2) mode should have smallest errors
Extrapolation errors should be smaller than resolution errors for well-converged simulations
non_negotiable_steps: Compare two highest resolutions for resolution error estimate
Decompose errors by spherical harmonic mode
Compare multiple extrapolation orders for extraction error estimate
Use minimal alignment (time and phase) before computing differences

checklist.modal_decomposition: DONE - fig7_data analyzed, ell=2 through ell=8
checklist.extrapolation_convergence: DONE - fig8_data analyzed, N2vsN3 and N2vsN4
